reason: Stock WebKit exposes a request's decoded text, not its original bytes (network.requestBody.bytes is unsupported there), so a 256-byte binary body can't be read back byte for byte

Stock WebKit refuses an empty or missing native text report, so it can't establish that a GET has no body (network.requestBody.absence is unsupported there), and the body read fails instead of giving None

A multipart/form-data body can't be read on Chromium or stock WebKit: Chromium's native report can omit a file and is refused (network.requestBody.multipart is unsupported there), and WebKit refuses multipart reports whose completeness it can't establish. Firefox reads the whole body

WebKitGTK's network process doesn't report the Cookie header, so a request's sent headers have no cookie there (network.headersSent is partial on stock WebKit). The matrix row method-request-allheaders says Strider has the full sent headers, which WebKit doesn't give
